title: Stovall's family and leaving the farm
summary: He was married 1947, divorced 1953, has sons and a daughter; he left the farm at 18 because he hated field work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I didn't get anything about your family. How many people were in your family?

Well, I was married, I don't have any kids, I've got two doctor sons, and I have a daughter. How old are you even married for them sometimes? I got married in 53. No, I'm sorry, I got divorced in 53. I was married in 47, yeah, 47. You know, the dates basically. Yeah, 47. And I was 16. And I got the date in 53.
How many in your family in Mississippi are those?

Well, we had a big family, of course, most of us, all of us did by now, we had a big family. I don't have any aunts or no uncles, nothing that type of living, a few cousins, that's right. I had one aunt there, but she's an in-law, she's a father. You had a couple brothers? Well, I've got some half brothers. I only had that whole brother. I got one half brother in Mississippi, and I got one here in the city, on my father's side.
And your father was a father? My father was dead.
Was he a father? Yeah, he was a father, yes. That's all he did in those days was father, in fact.
Yeah. I didn't have eyes, I never had eyes for it.

But I had to stay there because I was too young, I couldn't leave. And when I made 18, you better, I hiked out, I got out. Because I never liked it. I never could work in the field. They used to whip me by picking and kiting, I couldn't do it. I'd get on my knees, my knees get sore, I'd stand on my back, get sore. I never could make it. Yeah, I never could make it. Farming wasn't for me, I don't know. I couldn't think of it. So after I got to be in Maine, where I could give orders out of there. I got to get in a big house, I sent back to my mother and brother here. She passed here.
